title: Clip5
text:
Clip5 is a tiny window that stays on top of your other apps and holds five pieces of text. Click a slot’s button to copy its text to the clipboard, or the small × in the slot to clear it. Type or paste into a slot to change it. Everything is saved automatically.
Long text is shortened with “…” so the window stays small. Make the window taller to see more of each slot. Click a slot to see and edit all of it; while you’re editing, the slot scrolls instead. The Copy button always copies the full text. Spaces and blank lines around pasted text are removed automatically.

title: Clip5
text:
Download
Get the latest version from the Releases page.

Windows: download the .zip, right-click it, and choose Extract All. There’s nothing to install: move Clip5.exe wherever you like and double-click it. If Windows shows “Windows protected your PC”, click More info, then Run anyway. The app is free and not code-signed.
macOS: download and unzip the .zip, then drag Clip5.app into your Applications folder. The first time you open it, macOS can’t verify the developer. Click Done, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.

To update, replace the program with the new version. Your text is stored separately, so moving or replacing the program doesn’t affect it.

title: Clip5
text:
Open source
Clip5 is free and open source under the MIT licence. You’re welcome to download the code, change it, and build your own version.
In short:

Install Rust from rustup.rs. On Windows, accept the offer to install the Visual Studio C++ Build Tools. On macOS, run xcode-select --install first.
Get the code: download the ZIP from the GitHub repository (Code → Download ZIP), or open it with GitHub Desktop if you want updates and plan to contribute.
Run it: open a terminal in the Clip5 folder and type cargo run.
Build your own app: cargo build --release on Windows, or cargo bundle --release on macOS.

More details are in the README, including how to make changes and contribute.
